questions.answerHtml:
Comprehensive reference for Redis commands organized by category with real-world examples for connection testing, key management, and data operations.

Connection & Debugging

Testing Redis Connection with Telnet

Test connectivity to your Redis instance using telnet protocol.

# Install telnet (if not already installed)
sudo apt-get install telnet

# Connect to Redis instance
telnet instance-ip-address 6379

# In the telnet session, enter some Redis commands:
PING                  # Response: PONG
SET HELLO WORLD       # Response: +OK
GET HELLO             # Response: WORLD
DEL HELLO             # Response: :1 (number of deleted keys)
GET HELLO             # Response: $-1 (nil, key doesn't exist)
quit                  # Exit telnet session

Redis CLI Connection

Connect and test Redis using the official redis-cli tool.

# Connect to local Redis instance
redis-cli

# Connect to remote Redis instance
redis-cli -h instance-ip-address -p 6379

# Run command directly without entering CLI
redis-cli -h instance-ip-address PING

# Check connection with password
redis-cli -h instance-ip-address -a your-password PING

Key Management

SET - Store Key-Value

Set a key-value pair with optional expiration.

SET key value              # Set key to value
SET key value EX 3600      # Set with 60-minute expiration
SET key value PX 3600000   # Set with millisecond expiration
SET key value NX           # Set only if key doesn't exist
SET key value XX           # Set only if key exists

GET - Retrieve Value

Retrieve the value of a key.

GET key                    # Get value of key
GET non-existent-key       # Returns nil if key doesn't exist

DEL - Delete Keys

Delete one or more keys.

DEL key1                   # Delete single key
DEL key1 key2 key3         # Delete multiple keys
DEL non-existent-key       # Returns 0 (no keys deleted)

EXISTS - Check Key Existence

Check if one or more keys exist.

EXISTS key1                # Returns 1 if exists, 0 if not
EXISTS key1 key2 key3      # Returns count of existing keys

EXPIRE - Set Key Expiration

Set or modify key expiration time.

EXPIRE key 3600            # Set expiration to 60 minutes
PEXPIRE key 3600000        # Set expiration in milliseconds
TTL key                    # Get remaining time in seconds
PTTL key                   # Get remaining time in milliseconds
PERSIST key                # Remove expiration from key

Data Inspection

KEYS - Find Keys

Search for keys matching a pattern (use with caution in production).

KEYS *                     # List all keys
KEYS user:*                # Find keys starting with "user:"
KEYS *session*             # Find keys containing "session"
DBSIZE                     # Count total number of keys

TYPE - Get Value Type

Check the data type of a key.

TYPE key                   # Returns: string, list, set, zset, hash, etc.

INFO - Server Information

Get Redis server statistics and information.

INFO                       # All server information
INFO server                # Server details
INFO memory                # Memory usage
INFO stats                 # Command statistics
INFO replication           # Master/slave information

References

  • Testing connection of Redis using telnet
  • Redis Official Documentation
  • Redis Commands
  • Google Cloud Memorystore for Redis

questions.question: What are the common Redis caching patterns and strategies?
questions.searchLine: [devops • databases • memory-dbs • redis • database • caching • best • practices • pattern] What are the common Redis caching patterns and strategies?
questions.answerText: Redis caching patterns help optimize application performance and data consistency. Common patterns include Cache-Aside, Write-Through, and Write-Behind. Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading) Load data into cache only when necessary. Application checks cache first, and if data is missing, loads from database. 1. Application requests data from cache 2. Cache miss → Application loads from database 3. Application stores data in cache 4. Next requests get data from cache Pros: - Simple to implement - Only cached data is truly relevant - Resilient to cache failures Cons: - Cache misses cause application delay - Stale data possible if database changes - Cache stampede risk (many clients fetch same data) Write-Through Data is written to both cache and database simultaneously. 1. Application writes to cache 2. Cache writes to database (synchronously) 3. Acknowledgment returned to application Pros: - Data consistency guaranteed - Simple to understand - No stale data Cons: - Slower write operations - Write latency depends on database - Wasted cache space for never-read data Write-Behind (Write-Back) Data is written to cache first, database updated asynchronously. 1. Application writes to cache 2. Cache returns immediately (before DB write) 3. Background job writes to database Pros: - Fast write operations - Good for write-heavy workloads - Batches can be optimized Cons: - Risk of data loss if cache fails - Complex to implement correctly - Potential data inconsistency during failures References Caching Patterns - AWS Whitepaper Redis Caching Best Practices Cache Stampede Problem
questions.answerHtml:
Redis caching patterns help optimize application performance and data consistency. Common patterns include Cache-Aside, Write-Through, and Write-Behind.

Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading)

Load data into cache only when necessary. Application checks cache first, and if data is missing, loads from database.

1. Application requests data from cache
2. Cache miss → Application loads from database
3. Application stores data in cache
4. Next requests get data from cache

Pros:

  • Simple to implement
  • Only cached data is truly relevant
  • Resilient to cache failures

Cons:

  • Cache misses cause application delay
  • Stale data possible if database changes
  • Cache stampede risk (many clients fetch same data)

Write-Through

Data is written to both cache and database simultaneously.

1. Application writes to cache
2. Cache writes to database (synchronously)
3. Acknowledgment returned to application

Pros:

  • Data consistency guaranteed
  • Simple to understand
  • No stale data

Cons:

  • Slower write operations
  • Write latency depends on database
  • Wasted cache space for never-read data

Write-Behind (Write-Back)

Data is written to cache first, database updated asynchronously.

1. Application writes to cache
2. Cache returns immediately (before DB write)
3. Background job writes to database

Pros:

  • Fast write operations
  • Good for write-heavy workloads
  • Batches can be optimized

Cons:

  • Risk of data loss if cache fails
  • Complex to implement correctly
  • Potential data inconsistency during failures

References

  • Caching Patterns - AWS Whitepaper
  • Redis Caching Best Practices
  • Cache Stampede Problem

questions.answerHtml:
Comprehensive reference for Git commands organized by category with real-world examples.

Staging & Committing

git add

Add changes from working directory to staging area (Index).

git add <file>          # Stage specific file
git add .               # Stage all changes
git add -A              # Stage all changes including deletions
git add -p              # Stage changes interactively (patch mode)

git commit

Save staged changes as a permanent snapshot with a message.

git commit -m "[Feat] add user authentication"
git commit -am "Update documentation"
git commit --amend                  # Modify the last commit
git commit --amend --no-edit        # Add to last commit without changing message

Viewing Changes

git diff

Compare changes between working directory, staging area, and commits.

git diff                       # Unstaged changes since last commit
git diff --cached              # Staged changes (same as --staged)
git diff --staged              # Staged changes ready to commit
git diff HEAD                  # All changes since last commit
git diff master...contrib      # Changes in contrib branch vs master
git diff --word-diff           # Show changes at word level
git diff <commit1> <commit2>   # Compare two commits

git log

Display commit history with filtering and formatting options.

git log                                      # Full commit history
git log --oneline                            # Condensed format
git log -n 5                                 # Last 5 commits
git log --author=<author>                    # Commits by specific author
git log --since="2 weeks ago"                # Commits since date
git log --until="1 week ago"                 # Commits until date
git log --grep=<pattern>                     # Commits matching pattern
git log --follow <file>                      # History of file (including renames)
git log -p -- <file_path>                    # Changes to specific file
git log A..B                                 # Commits in B but not in A
git log --left-right A...B                   # Commits in A or B but not both
git log --abbrev-commit --no-merges          # Exclude merge commits
git log --pretty="format:%h %G? %aN   %s"   # Show GPG signatures

Branching

git branch

Create, list, and delete branches.

git branch                              # List local branches
git branch -a                           # List all branches (local + remote)
git branch <branch_name>                # Create new branch
git branch -d <branch_name>             # Delete branch (safe)
git branch -D <branch_name>             # Force delete branch
git branch -m <old_name> <new_name>    # Rename branch
git branch --track <branch> origin/<branch>  # Track remote branch

git checkout

Switch branches or restore files.

git checkout <branch>                          # Switch to branch
git checkout -b <branch>                       # Create and switch to branch
git checkout -b <branch> origin/<remote_branch> # Create from remote branch
git checkout -- <file>                         # Discard changes to file
git checkout <commit> -- <file>               # Restore file from commit

git switch

Modern alternative to checkout (Git 2.23+).

git switch <branch>            # Switch to branch
git switch -c <branch>         # Create and switch to branch
git switch -                   # Switch to previous branch

Merging & Rebasing

git merge

Combine branch history into current branch.

git merge <branch>                          # Simple merge
git merge --no-ff <branch>                  # Create merge commit
git merge --no-commit --squash <branch>     # Squash commits into one
git merge --abort                           # Cancel merge with conflicts
git merge --continue                        # Continue merge after resolving conflicts
git merge --strategy-option=ours            # Keep current version on conflicts

git rebase

Reapply commits on top of another branch (rewrites history).

git rebase <branch>                     # Rebase current branch
git rebase -i HEAD~3                    # Interactive rebase last 3 commits
git rebase --continue                   # Continue after resolving conflicts
git rebase --abort                      # Cancel rebase
git rebase --skip                       # Skip current commit during rebase

Stashing

git stash

Temporarily save changes without committing.

git stash                               # Save current changes
git stash save "description"            # Save with description
git stash list                          # List all stashes
git stash pop                           # Apply and remove latest stash
git stash apply stash@{0}              # Apply stash without removing
git stash drop stash@{0}               # Delete specific stash
git stash clear                         # Delete all stashes

Remote Operations

git fetch

Download changes from remote repository (no merge).

git fetch                               # Fetch from default remote
git fetch <remote>                      # Fetch from specific remote
git fetch --all                         # Fetch from all remotes
git fetch origin                        # Fetch from origin
git fetch origin refs/pull/958/head     # Fetch specific pull request
git fetch ../commits.bundle <branch>    # Fetch from bundle file

git pull

Fetch and merge changes from remote (fetch + merge).

git pull                                # Fetch and merge from remote
git pull origin <branch>                # Pull specific branch
git pull --rebase                       # Fetch and rebase instead of merge

git push

Upload commits to remote repository.

git push                                # Push to default remote
git push origin <branch>                # Push specific branch
git push origin --all                   # Push all branches
git push origin --tags                  # Push all tags
git push origin <branch> --force        # Force push (use carefully)
git push -u origin <branch>             # Push and set upstream

git remote

Manage remote repository references.

git remote                              # List remotes
git remote -v                           # List remotes with URLs
git remote add <name> <url>             # Add remote
git remote remove <name>                # Remove remote
git remote rename <old> <new>           # Rename remote
git remote set-url <name> <new_url>     # Change remote URL

History Inspection

git rev-parse

Get commit information and references.

git rev-parse develop                   # Get commit hash for branch
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD         # Get current branch name
git rev-parse HEAD                      # Get full hash of HEAD

git show

Display specific commit content.

git show <commit>                       # Show commit details
git show <commit>:<file>                # Show file at specific commit

Advanced Operations

git cherry-pick

Apply specific commits to current branch.

git cherry-pick <commit>                # Apply commit
git cherry-pick <commit1> <commit2>     # Apply multiple commits
git cherry-pick <commit>~..<commit>     # Apply range of commits
git cherry-pick --continue              # Continue after resolving conflicts
git cherry-pick --abort                 # Cancel cherry-pick

git bisect

Binary search through commits to find bug introduction.

git bisect start                        # Start bisect session
git bisect bad HEAD                     # Mark current as bad
git bisect good <commit>                # Mark commit as good
git bisect reset                        # Exit bisect mode

git clean

Remove untracked files from working directory.

git clean -n                            # Preview what would be deleted
git clean -f                            # Delete untracked files
git clean -fd                           # Delete untracked files and directories
git clean -fX                           # Delete only ignored files

git archive

Create archive (zip, tar) of project snapshot.

git archive HEAD --format=zip > project.zip
git archive <branch> --format=tar.gz > archive.tar.gz
git archive <branch> --prefix='project/' --format=zip > $(git describe <branch>).zip

git bundle

Package commits for transfer (useful offline).

git bundle create commits.bundle master ^9a466c5
git bundle create repo.bundle HEAD master
git bundle list-heads ../commits.bundle     # List branches in bundle
git bundle verify ../commits.bundle         # Verify bundle validity
git fetch ../commits.bundle <branch>        # Fetch from bundle
git clone repo.bundle repo                  # Clone from bundle

Configuration

git config

Set Git configuration options globally or per-repository.

# Identity
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "your@email.com"

# Editor
git config --global core.editor vim
git config --global core.pager less

# Colors
git config --global color.ui true
git config --global color.ui false         # Disable colors

# GPG Signing
git config --global user.signingkey <gpg-key-id>
git config commit.gpgsign true              # Enable signing
git config commit.gpgsign false             # Disable signing
git config --global gpg.program "$(which gpg)"

# Submodules
git config --global submodule.recurse false
git config --global diff.submodule log
git config -f .gitmodules submodule.[name].branch develop

# Aliases (shortcuts)
git config --global alias.co checkout
git config --global alias.br branch
git config --global alias.ci commit
git config --global alias.st status
git config alias.sdiff '!'"git diff && git submodule foreach 'git diff'"
git config alias.spush 'push --recurse-submodules=on-demand'
git config alias.supdate 'submodule update --remote --merge'

# View configuration
git config --list                           # Show all settings
git config --global --list                  # Show global settings
git config --global --edit                  # Edit global config
git config --global --unset <key>          # Unset specific setting

Tags

git tag

Create and manage version tags.

git tag                                 # List all tags
git tag <tag_name>                      # Create lightweight tag
git tag -a <tag_name> -m "message"     # Create annotated tag
git tag -a v1.2 9fceb02                # Tag specific commit
git tag -d <tag_name>                  # Delete tag locally
git push origin <tag_name>              # Push specific tag
git push origin --tags                  # Push all tags

Undoing Changes

Undo Strategies

# Discard changes (unstaged)
git checkout -- <file>
git restore <file>                      # Modern syntax

# Unstage changes
git reset HEAD <file>
git restore --staged <file>             # Modern syntax

# Undo last commit (keep changes)
git reset --soft HEAD~1

# Undo last commit (discard changes)
git reset --hard HEAD~1

# Revert specific commit (create new commit)
git revert <commit>

# Revert to specific commit
git reset --hard <commit>

Useful Patterns

Check what needs to be merged

git log --abbrev-commit --no-merges your_branch..origin/master
git log -n <number> your_branch..origin/master

See remote references

git ls-remote                           # All refs
git ls-remote | grep pull               # Pull requests
git ls-remote origin                    # Branch refs

Track remote branch

git checkout -b [local_branch] [remote]/[branch]
git branch --track <branch> origin/<branch>

Sync with remote after others pushed

git fetch origin
git merge origin/master
git push

View all changes before push

git diff --cached HEAD
git log origin/master..HEAD             # Commits not in remote

Best Practices

  1. Commit often - Logical, atomic commits are easier to review and debug
  2. Write meaningful messages - Follow commit message conventions
  3. Pull before push - Sync with remote before pushing
  4. Use branches - Develop features on separate branches
  5. Review before committing - Use git diff to verify changes
  6. Clean up branches - Delete merged branches to keep repo tidy
  7. Sign commits - Use GPG signing for security
  8. Use tags for releases - Annotated tags for production versions
  9. Document workflow - Keep team aligned on branching strategy
  10. Backup before force push - --force rewrites history, be careful

Common Workflows

Feature Branch Workflow

git checkout -b feature/my-feature       # Create feature branch
# Make changes...
git add .
git commit -m "[Feat] implement feature"
git push -u origin feature/my-feature
# Create pull request
# After review and merge:
git checkout main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feature/my-feature

Release Branch Workflow

git checkout -b release/v1.0             # Create release branch
# Fix bugs only
git commit -m "[Fix] critical bug"
git push origin release/v1.0
# After testing:
git checkout main
git merge --no-ff release/v1.0
git tag -a v1.0 -m "Release v1.0"
git push origin main --tags

Hotfix Workflow

git checkout -b hotfix/critical-bug      # Branch from main
git commit -m "[Fix] critical production issue"
git push origin hotfix/critical-bug

questions.answerHtml:
Follow these conventions for clear, searchable, and maintainable commit history.

Commit Message Format

<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body>

<footer>

Commit Types

[Add] - New addition

Use when introducing new files or features that don't fit other categories.

git commit -m "[Add] new user authentication module"
git commit -m "[Add] database migration script for schema v2"
git commit -m "[Add] API endpoint for user profile"

[Build] - Build system changes

Changes affecting the build, CI/CD pipelines, or external dependencies.

git commit -m "[Build] update webpack configuration for production"
git commit -m "[Build] configure GitHub Actions workflow"
git commit -m "[Build] add Docker build multi-stage optimization"

[Chore] - Dependency updates

Updates to dependencies, tooling, or maintenance tasks.

git commit -m "[Chore] upgrade npm dependencies to latest versions"
git commit -m "[Chore] update Python package requirements"
git commit -m "[Chore] bump Node.js version to 18.x"

[CiCd] - CI/CD pipeline changes

Continuous integration and continuous delivery related changes.

git commit -m "[CiCd] add automated deployment pipeline"
git commit -m "[CiCd] configure test coverage reporting"
git commit -m "[CiCd] add pre-commit linting hooks"

[Docs] - Documentation updates

Updates to README, markdown files, or code comments.

git commit -m "[Docs] update installation instructions in README"
git commit -m "[Docs] add API documentation for authentication"
git commit -m "[Docs] improve code comments for utility functions"

[Feat] - New feature

A new feature is introduced with the changes.

git commit -m "[Feat] implement dark mode toggle"
git commit -m "[Feat] add search functionality with filters"
git commit -m "[Feat] support OAuth2 authentication"

[Fix] - Bug fix

A bug fix has occurred.

git commit -m "[Fix] resolve memory leak in event listener cleanup"
git commit -m "[Fix] correct calculation in billing module"
git commit -m "[Fix] handle null reference in data parser"

[Improvement] - Enhancement

Improvements or enhancements to existing functionality.

git commit -m "[Improvement] enhance search performance with caching"
git commit -m "[Improvement] optimize database queries for reports"
git commit -m "[Improvement] streamline user onboarding flow"

[Perf] - Performance improvements

Optimizations that improve speed or resource usage.

git commit -m "[Perf] reduce bundle size by 40%"
git commit -m "[Perf] optimize image loading with lazy loading"
git commit -m "[Perf] cache API responses for 5 minutes"

[Refactor] - Code refactoring

Refactored code that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature.

git commit -m "[Refactor] extract duplicate logic into helper functions"
git commit -m "[Refactor] simplify conditional statements with early returns"
git commit -m "[Refactor] reorganize module structure for clarity"

[Release] - Release notes

Version release or release-related changes.

git commit -m "[Release] v1.2.0 - add authentication and performance improvements"
git commit -m "[Release] v2.0.0 - breaking: migrate to new API schema"

[Remove] - Removal

Remove functions, temporary files, deprecated code, or unused features.

git commit -m "[Remove] delete deprecated API endpoints"
git commit -m "[Remove] clean up temporary test fixtures"
git commit -m "[Remove] remove legacy browser compatibility code"

[Revert] - Revert previous commit

Reverts a previous commit (use sparingly, prefer explicit fixes).

git commit -m "[Revert] revert '[Feat] add A/B testing feature' (caused production issue)"
git commit -m "[Revert] revert commit abc1234 due to merge conflict"

[Style] - Code formatting

Related to code formatting such as whitespace, missing semi-colons, and similar cosmetic changes.

git commit -m "[Style] format code with Prettier"
git commit -m "[Style] add missing semicolons"
git commit -m "[Style] adjust indentation for consistency"

[Test] - Testing changes

Including new, correcting previous, or improving tests.

git commit -m "[Test] add unit tests for payment module"
git commit -m "[Test] fix flaky integration test for API"
git commit -m "[Test] increase test coverage to 85%"

[Update] - General updates

General updates or changes that don't fit specific categories.

git commit -m "[Update] change user profile default avatar"
git commit -m "[Update] modify configuration for staging environment"
git commit -m "[Update] refresh vendor libraries"

Best Practices

  1. Use imperative mood - "add feature" not "added feature"
  2. Keep subject line under 50 characters - Concise and scannable
  3. Separate subject from body with blank line - Easier to read in logs
  4. Wrap body at 72 characters - Better formatted in terminals
  5. Explain what and why, not how - Implementation details should be clear from code
  6. Use lowercase for type - Consistency across commits
  7. No period at end of subject - Convention in many projects
  8. Reference issues and PRs - Link to tracking systems: "Fixes #123" or "Relates to PR #456"

Extended Commit Example

git commit -m "[Feat] add OAuth2 authentication support

- Implement Google OAuth2 provider integration
- Add JWT token generation and validation
- Support refresh token rotation for security
- Create user session management module

Closes #234
Relates to milestone v2.0

Conventional Commits Standard

For stricter formatting, use Conventional Commits format:

git commit -m "feat(auth): add OAuth2 support

Implement OAuth2 authentication with Google provider.
Supports automatic token refresh and secure session handling.

BREAKING CHANGE: Legacy token format is no longer supported
Closes #234

Commit Frequency

  • Frequent, logical commits - One feature/fix per commit when possible
  • Atomic changes - Each commit should be independently deployable
  • Meaningful history - Commits tell a story of development decisions

Tools to Help

  • commitizen - Interactive commit message generator
  • husky + lint-staged - Enforce commit message standards
  • conventional-commits - Strict format validation
  • git-aliases - Create shortcuts for common patterns

Example .gitconfig alias:

git config --global alias.feat '!git commit -m "[Feat]"'
git config --global alias.fix '!git commit -m "[Fix]"'
git config --global alias.docs '!git commit -m "[Docs]"'

Usage: ``bash git feat "add new login form" # [Feat] add new login form git fix "handle null pointer" # [Fix] handle null pointer git docs "update API reference" # [Docs] update API reference ``

questions.answerHtml:
Comprehensive reference for Windows Command Prompt and PowerShell commands organized by category for system administration, diagnostics, and troubleshooting.

System Information & Health

systeminfo

Display detailed system configuration and hardware information.

systeminfo                                          # Show all system info
systeminfo | findstr /C:"OS Name"                  # Show Windows version
wmic os get caption                                 # Get Windows edition
wmic cpu get name                                   # Show CPU model
wmic cpu get NumberOfCores                          # Show CPU cores
wmic memorychip get capacity                        # Show RAM modules
Get-ComputerInfo                                    # PowerShell system info

System File Checker (sfc)

Scan and repair corrupted system files.

sfc /scannow                                        # Scan and repair system files
sfc /verifyonly                                     # Scan without repair
sfc /scanfile=<filepath>                           # Scan specific file

DISM (Deployment Image Servicing Management)

Repair Windows component store and image health.

DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth           # Quick health check
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth            # Detailed scan
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth         # Repair Windows components
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup # Clean up old components

chkdsk

Check disk for errors and bad sectors.

chkdsk C:                                           # Check disk (read-only)
chkdsk C: /F                                        # Fix errors on next boot
chkdsk C: /F /R                                     # Scan and repair bad sectors
chkdsk C: /V                                        # Verbose output

Event Logs & Monitoring

Event Logging Tools

View and manage Windows Event Log channels.

wevtutil el                                         # List all event log channels
wevtutil qe System /c:20 /f:text                   # Show last 20 system events
wevtutil cl System                                  # Clear System log
Get-EventLog -LogName System -Newest 50             # PowerShell: last 50 system logs
Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -MaxEvents 20       # PowerShell: security logs
Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; Level=2}  # Error events only

Performance Counters

Monitor real-time system performance metrics.

Get-Counter '\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time'  # CPU usage
Get-Counter '\Memory\Available MBytes'              # Available RAM
Get-Counter '\Memory\% Committed Bytes In Use'     # Memory utilization
Get-Counter '\Network Interface(*)\Bytes Total/sec' # Network throughput
Get-Counter '\LogicalDisk(C:)\% Disk Time'        # Disk usage
typeperf -cf counters.txt -o output.csv            # Log performance over time

Process Management

tasklist & taskkill

View and terminate running processes.

tasklist                                            # List running processes
tasklist /v                                         # Detailed process list
tasklist /v | findstr python                       # Find specific process
taskkill /PID 1234 /F                              # Kill by PID (force)
taskkill /IM notepad.exe /F                        # Kill by name
Get-Process                                         # PowerShell: list processes
Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending          # Top CPU consumers
Get-Process | Sort-Object WorkingSet -Descending   # Top RAM consumers
Stop-Process -Name notepad -Force                  # PowerShell: kill process

Services Management

sc (Service Control)

Manage Windows services from command line.

sc query                                            # List all services
sc query <service>                                  # Check specific service
sc start <service>                                  # Start service
sc stop <service>                                   # Stop service
sc config <service> start= auto                    # Auto-start on boot
sc config <service> start= demand                  # Manual start
sc config <service> start= disabled                # Disable service
sc delete <service>                                 # Delete service
sc query state= all                                # List all services (any state)

PowerShell Service Cmdlets

Manage services with PowerShell.

Get-Service                                         # List all services
Get-Service -Name <service>                        # Get specific service
Start-Service -Name <service>                      # Start service
Stop-Service -Name <service>                       # Stop service
Restart-Service -Name <service>                    # Restart service
Set-Service -Name <service> -StartupType Automatic # Set auto-start

Drivers Management

Driver Query & Management

List and manage installed drivers.

driverquery                                         # List drivers
driverquery /v                                      # Detailed driver info
driverquery /si                                     # Driver signing info
pnputil /enum-drivers                              # List driver packages
pnputil /delete-driver oem12.inf /uninstall       # Remove driver package
Get-WmiObject Win32_SystemDriver                   # PowerShell: system drivers

Networking

ipconfig

Display and configure network settings.

ipconfig                                            # Show IP configuration
ipconfig /all                                       # Full network details
ipconfig /renew                                     # Renew DHCP lease
ipconfig /flushdns                                  # Clear DNS cache
ipconfig /registerdns                              # Register DNS with domain
ipconfig /release                                  # Release DHCP lease
Get-NetIPAddress                                    # PowerShell: IP addresses
Get-NetAdapter                                      # Show network adapters

Connectivity Testing

Test network connectivity and DNS resolution.

ping hostname                                       # Test connectivity
ping 8.8.8.8                                        # Test internet connectivity
tracert hostname                                    # Trace network route
tracert -d hostname                                 # Trace (IP only)
nslookup hostname                                   # DNS lookup
nslookup -type=MX domain.com                       # Query MX records

Get-NetDnsConfiguration                             # Show DNS settings
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName server -Port 443  # Test specific port

netstat

Display active network connections and listening ports.

netstat -ano                                        # All connections with PID
netstat -ano | findstr :443                        # Check if port is listening
netstat -ab                                         # Show process names
netstat -an | findstr ESTABLISHED                  # Show established connections
Get-NetTCPConnection                                # PowerShell: TCP connections
Get-NetUDPEndpoint                                  # PowerShell: UDP endpoints

Firewall Management

Manage Windows Firewall rules.

netsh advfirewall firewall show rule name=all      # Show all firewall rules
netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="Allow80" protocol=tcp dir=in action=allow localport=80
netsh advfirewall firewall delete rule name="Allow80"  # Delete rule
netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state on         # Enable firewall
netsh advfirewall reset                             # Reset to defaults
Get-NetFirewallRule                                 # PowerShell: list rules
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Allow80" -Direction Inbound -Action Allow -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 80

Routing

Configure network routing.

route print                                         # Show routing table
route add 10.0.0.0 mask 255.255.255.0 10.0.1.1   # Add static route
route delete 10.0.0.0 mask 255.255.255.0           # Delete route
route -p add 10.0.0.0 mask 255.255.255.0 10.0.1.1 # Add persistent route
Get-NetRoute                                        # PowerShell: routing table

Disk & Storage Management

diskpart

Partition and volume management tool.

diskpart                                            # Open diskpart (then use below inside)
list disk                                           # List all disks
list volume                                         # List volumes
list partition                                      # List partitions
select disk 1                                       # Select disk
clean                                               # Wipe disk
create partition primary size=<MB>                 # Create partition
format fs=NTFS label="Data"                        # Format volume
assign letter=D                                     # Assign drive letter

PowerShell Disk Cmdlets

Manage disks and volumes with PowerShell.

Get-Disk                                            # List disks
Get-Partition                                       # List partitions
Get-Volume                                          # List volumes
Resize-Partition -DriveLetter C -Size 100GB        # Resize partition
Format-Volume -DriveLetter E -FileSystem NTFS -Force  # Format volume
New-Partition -DiskNumber 1 -Size 50GB -DriveLetter F  # Create partition

Users & Group Management

Local User & Group Management

Manage local accounts and groups.

net user                                            # List local users
net user <username>                                 # Show user details
net user <username> <password> /add                # Create local user
net user <username> /delete                        # Delete local user
net localgroup                                      # List local groups
net localgroup Administrators                      # Show admin group members
net localgroup Administrators <username> /add      # Add user to admin group
net localgroup Administrators <username> /delete   # Remove from admin group
whoami                                              # Show current user
whoami /groups                                      # Show user groups
whoami /priv                                        # Show privileges
Get-LocalUser                                       # PowerShell: list users
Get-LocalGroup                                      # PowerShell: list groups
Add-LocalGroupMember -Group Administrators -Member <user>  # Add to group

Registry Management

Registry Editing

Query and modify Windows Registry.

reg query HKLM\Software                             # Query registry key
reg add HKLM\Software\Test /v Setting /t REG_SZ /d 123 /f  # Add value
reg delete HKLM\Software\Test /v Setting /f        # Delete value
reg export HKLM\Software software.reg              # Export registry
reg import software.reg                             # Import registry
reg load HKLM\Temp C:\path\to\hive                # Load hive file
reg unload HKLM\Temp                               # Unload hive
Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion"  # PowerShell
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\Software\Test" -Name "Setting" -Value "123"
Remove-Item -Path "HKLM:\Software\Test" -Recurse  # Delete registry key

Boot & Shutdown

Boot Configuration

Manage boot options and safe mode.

bcdedit                                             # Show boot configuration
bcdedit /set {default} safeboot minimal            # Boot to Safe Mode
bcdedit /set {default} safeboot network            # Safe Mode with Networking
bcdedit /deletevalue {default} safeboot            # Remove Safe Mode
bcdedit /set {default} numproc 4                   # Set number of cores

Shutdown & Restart

Schedule or execute system shutdown/restart.

shutdown /r /t 0                                    # Restart immediately
shutdown /s /t 0                                    # Shutdown immediately
shutdown /s /t 300                                  # Shutdown after 300 seconds
shutdown /a                                         # Abort shutdown/restart
shutdown /h                                         # Hibernate
shutdown /g /t 0                                    # Restart and restart apps

Domain Controller Commands

Active Directory and domain diagnostics.

nltest /dsgetdc:domain.local                       # Discover domain controller
nltest /dclist:domain.local                        # List DCs in domain
nltest /sc_verify:domain.local                     # Verify secure channel
nltest /sc_reset:domain.local                      # Reset secure channel
Get-ADDomain                                        # PowerShell: domain info
Get-ADForest                                        # PowerShell: forest info
Get-ADDomainController -Filter *                   # List all DCs
Get-ADDomainController -Discover                   # Find nearest DC

Query and manage AD objects.

Get-ADUser <username> -Properties *                # Get user properties
Get-ADComputer <computername> -Properties *        # Get computer properties
Get-ADObject -LDAPFilter "(objectClass=computer)"  # LDAP query
Move-ADObject -Identity "CN=VM01,OU=Computers,DC=domain,DC=local" -TargetPath "OU=Servers,DC=domain,DC=local"  # Move to OU

repadmin /replsummary                              # Replication summary
repadmin /showrepl                                  # Detailed replication status
repadmin /syncall /AeD                             # Force full replication
dcdiag /v                                           # Full DC diagnostics
dcdiag /test:sysvolcheck                           # Check SYSVOL health
dcdiag /test:advertising                           # Check DC advertising status

DNS Resolution

nslookup <hostname>                                 # DNS lookup
nslookup -type=A domain.com                        # Query A record
nslookup -type=MX domain.com                       # Query MX record

Resolve-DnsName -Type MX domain.com                # Query MX records
Resolve-DnsName -Type SRV _kerberos._tcp.domain.local  # Query SRV records
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName dc01 -Port 53    # Test DNS port

Remove-DnsServerResourceRecord -ZoneName domain.local -RRType A -Name "server1" -Force  # Delete A record
dnscmd /enumzones                                   # List zones (legacy)
dnscmd /zoneinfo domain.local                      # Zone information
dnscmd /clearcache                                  # Clear server cache

Virtual Machine Management

Manage Hyper-V virtual machines.

Get-VM                                              # List all VMs
Get-VM -Name "VM01"                                # Get specific VM
Start-VM -Name "VM01"                              # Start VM

Stop-VM -Name "VM01" -Force                        # Force stop VM

IIS Management

Install and configure Internet Information Services.

questions.answerHtml:
Why "Know" vs "Don't Know" Is Not Enough

Vocabulary knowledge is not binary.

Know
Don't Know

This classification is too simplistic because understanding a word and actively using a word are very different skills.

A better approach is to classify vocabulary into five levels.

Level 0 — Unknown

I don't know the meaning of the word.

Examples

whereas
venue

Characteristics

  • Never seen it before
  • Cannot guess the meaning
  • Cannot use it

Level 1 — Familiar

I've seen the word before.

Example

transition

Characteristics

  • Looks familiar
  • Might vaguely remember seeing it
  • Not sure of the meaning
  • Cannot use it

Level 2 — Passive Recognition

I understand the word when reading or listening.

Example

The company is going through a transition period.

Characteristics

  • Understand it in context
  • Can read articles containing it
  • Can understand it when hearing it
  • Cannot easily create my own sentence

Level 3 — Controlled Production

I can use the word if I have time to think.

Example

We are in a transition phase.

Characteristics

  • Can write with it
  • Can use it if given enough time
  • Does not naturally appear in conversations
  • Does not automatically appear during meetings

Level 4 — Active Vocabulary

The word comes naturally when speaking or writing.

Examples

problem
meeting
project
manager
customer

Characteristics

  • No conscious effort required
  • Used naturally in speaking
  • Used naturally in writing
  • Available immediately during conversations

Quick Self-Test

For every word, ask yourself:

Question 1

Do I know the meaning?

Yes / No

Question 2

Can I make a sentence within 5 seconds?

Example:

Doctors urge people to exercise regularly.

Question 3

Would I naturally use this word during a conversation or work meeting?

If Yes

Level 4

If I need time to think

Level 3

If I only recognize it while reading or listening

Level 2

Vocabulary Tracking Spreadsheet

Word | Level

Example:

problem       | 4
meeting       | 4
roadmap       | 3
stakeholder   | 3
urge          | 2
venue         | 2
sympathy      | 2
whereas       | 1

Where to Focus

Do NOT spend most of your time on Level 0 words.

The highest return on investment comes from moving words from:

Level 2 → Level 4

Examples:

stakeholder
ownership
transition
surround
sympathy
venue
urge

These words are already known.

The problem is that they are not yet part of my active vocabulary.

Using AI to Activate Vocabulary

Create a list like this:

Words to activate:

stakeholder
ownership
transition
surround
urge
venue
sympathy

Use the following prompt when chatting with AI:

When replying in English, try to use the following words whenever appropriate:

stakeholder
ownership
transition
surround
urge
venue
sympathy

Highlight any of these words in bold.

Use natural native-level English.

Over time, repeated exposure moves the words through the stages:

Level 2
↓
Level 3
↓
Level 4

Long-Term Goal

Target distribution:

Level 4 (Active Vocabulary):      ~2,000 words

Level 3 (Semi-Active Vocabulary): ~2,000 words

Level 2 (Passive Vocabulary):     ~2,000+ words

You do NOT need 8,000 active words.

A practical target is:

2,000 active words
+
2,000 semi-active words

This is usually enough to communicate comfortably in international engineering and management environments.

Type: Verb (v.) - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /əˈbændən/ - English Meaning: To leave something or someone permanently. - Vietnamese Meaning: Từ bỏ; bỏ lại. - Example: They abandoned the project because it was too expensive. - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /ədˈmaɪər/ - English Meaning: To respect or like someone greatly. - Vietnamese Meaning: Ngưỡng mộ; khâm phục. - Example: I admire her determination and hard work. - Example Translation: Tôi ngưỡng mộ sự quyết tâm và chăm chỉ của cô ấy. 41. admit - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /ədˈmɪt/ - English Meaning: To agree that something is true. - Vietnamese Meaning: Thừa nhận. - Example: She admitted that she was wrong. - Example Translation: Cô ấy thừa nhận rằng mình đã sai. 42. adopt - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ədˈvæntɪdʒ/ - English Meaning: A condition that helps you succeed. - Vietnamese Meaning: Lợi thế. - Example: Experience gives you an advantage in the job market. - Example Translation: Kinh nghiệm mang lại cho bạn lợi thế trên thị trường lao động. 47. adventure - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ədˈventʃər/ - English Meaning: An exciting and unusual experience. - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ˈædvərtaɪz/ - English Meaning: To promote a product or service. - Vietnamese Meaning: Quảng cáo. - Example: The company advertised its new product on television. - Example Translation: Công ty quảng cáo sản phẩm mới trên truyền hình. 49. advertisement - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ˌædvərˈtaɪzmənt/ - English Meaning: A message that promotes a product or service. - Vietnamese Meaning: Quảng cáo. - Example: I saw an interesting advertisement online. - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /əˈfekt/ - English Meaning: To influence something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Ảnh hưởng. - Example: Lack of sleep can affect your concentration. - Example Translation: Thiếu ngủ có thể ảnh hưởng đến sự tập trung của bạn. 55. afford - Type: Adverb - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /ˈæftərwərd/ - English Meaning: Later, after something else happens. - Vietnamese Meaning: Sau đó. - Example: We had dinner and afterward watched a movie. - Example Translation: Chúng tôi ăn tối và sau đó xem phim. 60. again - Type: Noun, Verb - CEFR Level: A1, B1 - IPA (US): /eɪdʒ/ - English Meaning: The number of years someone has lived. - Vietnamese Meaning: Tuổi tác. - Example: She started piano lessons at the age of six. - Type: Adjective - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /əˈɡresɪv/ - English Meaning: Ready to fight or compete strongly. - Vietnamese Meaning: Hung hăng; quyết liệt. - Example: The company launched an aggressive marketing campaign. - Vietnamese Meaning: Đồng ý. - Example: I agree with your opinion. - Example Translation: Tôi đồng ý với ý kiến của bạn. 69. agreement - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /əˈɡriːmənt/ - English Meaning: A decision accepted by all sides. - viện trợ. - Example: International aid arrived after the disaster. - Example Translation: Viện trợ quốc tế đã đến sau thảm họa. 74. aim - Type: Noun, Verb - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /eɪm/ - English Meaning: A goal or purpose. - Vietnamese Meaning: Mục tiêu. - Example: Our aim is to provide excellent service. - Example Translation: Mục tiêu của chúng tôi là cung cấp dịch vụ xuất sắc. 75. air - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /er/ - English Meaning: The invisible mixture of gases around Earth. - Vietnamese Meaning: Không khí. - Example: Let's go outside and get some fresh air. - Example Translation: Hãy ra ngoài hít thở không khí trong lành. 76. aircraft - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /ˈerkræft/ - English Meaning: A vehicle designed to fly. - Vietnamese Meaning: Máy bay; được. - Example: Everything will be all right. - Example Translation: Mọi chuyện sẽ ổn thôi. 86. allow - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /əˈlaʊ/ - English Meaning: To let someone do something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Cho phép. - Example: The teacher allowed questions. - Example Translation: Giáo viên cho phép đặt câu hỏi. 87. almost - Type: Adverb - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ˈɔːlmoʊst/ - English Meaning: Very nearly but not completely. - Vietnamese Meaning: Gần như. - Example: I have almost finished my homework. - Example Translation: Tôi gần như hoàn thành bài tập về nhà. 88. alone - Type: Adjective, Adverb - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /əˈloʊn/ - English Meaning: Without other people. - Vietnamese Meaning: Một mình. - Example: She prefers to travel alone. - Example Translation: Cô ấy thích đi du lịch một mình. 89. along - Type: Preposition, Adverb - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /əˈlɔːŋ/ - English Meaning: Moving beside or following something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Dọc theo. - Example: We walked along the river. - Example Translation: Chúng tôi đi bộ dọc theo con sông. 90. already - Type: Adverb - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ɔːlˈredi/ - English Meaning: Before now or sooner than expected. - Vietnamese Meaning: Đã; rồi. - Example: I've already seen that movie. - Example Translation: Tôi đã xem bộ phim đó rồi. 91. also - Type: Adverb - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /ˈɔːlsoʊ/ - English Meaning: In addition. - Vietnamese Meaning: Cũng; questions.answerHtml:
Words 1 to 100 from the Oxford 3000 list - the 3000 most important words to learn in English from A1 to B2 level.

1. a, an

  • Type: Indefinite Article
  • CEFR Level: A1
  • IPA (US): /ə/, /eɪ/; /ən/, /æn/
  • English Meaning: Used before a singular countable noun.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Một; một người; một vật.
  • Example: She bought a book and an orange.
  • Example Translation: Cô ấy đã mua một quyển sách và một quả cam.

2. abandon

  • Type: Verb (v.)
  • CEFR Level: B2
  • IPA (US): /əˈbændən/
  • English Meaning: To leave something or someone permanently.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Từ bỏ; bỏ lại.
  • Example: They abandoned the project because it was too expensive.
  • Example Translation: Họ từ bỏ dự án vì quá tốn kém.

3. ability

  • Type: Noun (n.)
  • CEFR Level: A2
  • IPA (US): /əˈbɪləti/
  • English Meaning: The power or skill to do something.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Khả năng; năng lực.
  • Example: She has the ability to solve difficult problems.
  • Example Translation: Cô ấy có khả năng giải quyết những vấn đề khó.

4. able

  • Type: Adjective (adj.)
  • CEFR Level: A2
  • IPA (US): /ˈeɪbəl/
  • English Meaning: Having the power or skill to do something.

April - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /ˈeɪprəl/ - English Meaning: The fourth month of the year. - Vietnamese Meaning: Tháng Tư. - Example: My birthday is in April. - Example Translation: Sinh nhật của tôi vào tháng Tư. 148. architect - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ˈɑːrkətekt/ - English Meaning: A person who designs buildings. - Vietnamese Meaning: Kiến trúc sư. - Example: She works as an architect. - Example Translation: Cô ấy làm kiến trúc sư. 149. architecture - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ˈɑːrkətektʃər/ - English Meaning: The design and style of buildings. - Vietnamese Meaning: Kiến trúc. - Example: The city's architecture is beautiful. - Example Translation: Kiến trúc của thành phố rất đẹp. 150. area - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /ˈeriə/ - English Meaning: A particular place or region. - Vietnamese Meaning: Khu vực; vùng. - Example: This area is very quiet. - Example Translation: Khu vực này rất yên tĩnh. 151. argue - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ˈɑːrɡjuː/ - English Meaning: To disagree with someone. - Vietnamese Meaning: Tranh cãi. - Example: They often argue about money. - Example Translation: Họ thường tranh cãi về tiền bạc. 152. argument - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ˈɑːrɡjəmənt/ - English Meaning: A disagreement between people. - Vietnamese Meaning: Cuộc tranh cãi. - Example: They had an argument yesterday. - Example Translation: Họ đã có một cuộc tranh cãi hôm qua. 153. arise - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /əˈraɪz/ - English Meaning: To happen or begin to exist. - Vietnamese Meaning: Phát sinh; nảy sinh. - Example: Problems may arise during the project. - Example Translation: Các vấn đề có thể phát sinh trong dự án. 154. arm - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /ɑːrm/ - English Meaning: The part of the body between the shoulder and hand. - Vietnamese Meaning: Cánh tay. - Example: He hurt his arm while playing sports. - Example Translation: Anh ấy bị đau cánh tay khi chơi thể thao. 155. armed - Type: Adjective - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /ɑːrmd/ - English Meaning: Carrying weapons. - Vietnamese Meaning: Có vũ trang. - Example: Armed guards protected the building. - Example Translation: Những người bảo vệ có vũ trang bảo vệ tòa nhà. 156. arms - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /ɑːrmz/ - English Meaning: Weapons used in fighting. - Vietnamese Meaning: Vũ khí. - Example: The country reduced its arms production. - Example Translation: Quốc gia này đã giảm sản xuất vũ khí. 157. army - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ˈɑːrmi/ - English Meaning: A country's military force. - Vietnamese Meaning: Quân đội. - Example: He joined the army at eighteen. - Example Translation: Anh ấy nhập ngũ khi mười tám tuổi. 158. around - Type: Preposition, Adverb - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /əˈraʊnd/ - English Meaning: On every side of something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Xung quanh. - Example: We walked around the park. - Example Translation: Chúng tôi đi bộ quanh công viên. 159. arrange - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /əˈreɪndʒ/ - English Meaning: To organize or plan something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Sắp xếp. - Example: She arranged a meeting with the client. - Example Translation: Cô ấy đã sắp xếp một cuộc họp với khách hàng. 160. arrangement - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /əˈreɪndʒmənt/ - English Meaning: A plan or organization of something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Sự sắp xếp; thỏa thuận. - Example: We made travel arrangements in advance. - Example Translation: Chúng tôi đã sắp xếp chuyến đi từ trước. 161. arrest - Type: Noun, Verb - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /əˈrest/ - English Meaning: To take someone into legal custody. - Vietnamese Meaning: Bắt giữ; sự bắt giữ. - Example: Police arrested the suspect. - Example Translation: Cảnh sát đã bắt giữ nghi phạm. 162. arrival - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /əˈraɪvəl/ - English Meaning: The act of reaching a place. - Vietnamese Meaning: Sự đến nơi. - Example: We waited for her arrival. - Example Translation: Chúng tôi đợi cô ấy đến. 163. arrive - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /əˈraɪv/ - English Meaning: To reach a place. - Vietnamese Meaning: Đến nơi. - Example: We arrived at the station early. - Example Translation: Chúng tôi đến nhà ga sớm. 164. art - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /ɑːrt/ - English Meaning: Creative works such as paintings and music. - Vietnamese Meaning: Nghệ thuật. - Example: She studies art at university. - Example Translation: Cô ấy học nghệ thuật tại trường đại học. 165. article - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /ˈɑːrtɪkəl/ - English Meaning: A piece of writing in a newspaper or website. - Vietnamese Meaning: Bài báo. - Example: I read an interesting article online. - Example Translation: Tôi đã đọc một bài báo thú vị trên mạng. 166. artificial - Type: Adjective - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /ˌɑːrtɪˈfɪʃəl/ - English Meaning: Made by humans, not natural. - Vietnamese Meaning: Nhân tạo. - Example: The flowers are artificial. - Example Translation: Những bông hoa này là hoa nhân tạo. 167. artist - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /ˈɑːrtɪst/ - English Meaning: A person who creates art. - Vietnamese Meaning: Nghệ sĩ. - Example: The artist displayed her paintings. - Example Translation: Người nghệ sĩ đã trưng bày các bức tranh của mình. 168. artistic - Type: Adjective - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /ɑːrˈtɪstɪk/ - English Meaning: Related to art or creativity. - Vietnamese Meaning: Có tính nghệ thuật. - Example: She has strong artistic talent. - Example Translation: Cô ấy có tài năng nghệ thuật nổi bật. 169. as - Type: Preposition, Adverb, Conjunction - CEFR Level: A1, A2 - IPA (US): /æz/, /əz/ - English Meaning: Used to compare or explain something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Như; khi; bởi vì. - Example: She works as a teacher. - Example Translation: Cô ấy làm việc như một giáo viên. 170. ashamed - Type: Adjective - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /əˈʃeɪmd/ - English Meaning: Feeling guilty or embarrassed. - Vietnamese Meaning: Xấu hổ. - Example: He felt ashamed of his behavior. - Example Translation: Anh ấy cảm thấy xấu hổ về hành vi của mình. 171. aside - Type: Adverb - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /əˈsaɪd/ - English Meaning: To one side or out of the way. - Vietnamese Meaning: Sang một bên. - Example: She stepped aside to let people pass. - Example Translation: Cô ấy bước sang một bên để mọi người đi qua. 172. asleep - Type: Adjective - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /əˈsliːp/ - English Meaning: Sleeping. - Vietnamese Meaning: Đang ngủ. - Example: The baby is asleep. - Example Translation: Đứa bé đang ngủ. 173. ask - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /æsk/ - English Meaning: To request information or help. - Vietnamese Meaning: Hỏi; yêu cầu. - Example: I want to ask a question. - Example Translation: Tôi muốn đặt một câu hỏi. 174. aspect - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /ˈæspekt/ - English Meaning: A particular part of something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Khía cạnh. - Example: We discussed every aspect of the project. - Example Translation: Chúng tôi đã thảo luận mọi khía cạnh của dự án. 175. assess - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /əˈses/ - English Meaning: To evaluate or judge something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Đánh giá. - Example: Teachers assess students regularly. - Example Translation: Giáo viên đánh giá học sinh thường xuyên. 176. assessment - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /əˈsesmənt/ - English Meaning: The act of evaluating something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Sự đánh giá. - Example: The assessment took two hours. - Example Translation: Việc đánh giá kéo dài hai giờ. 177. assignment - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /əˈsaɪnmənt/ - English Meaning: A task given to someone. - Vietnamese Meaning: Bài tập; nhiệm vụ. - Example: I completed my assignment yesterday. - Example Translation: Tôi đã hoàn thành bài tập hôm qua. 178. assist - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /əˈsɪst/ - English Meaning: To help someone. - Vietnamese Meaning: Hỗ trợ; giúp đỡ. - Example: Staff members assisted the visitors. - Example Translation: Nhân viên đã hỗ trợ khách tham quan. 179. assistant - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /əˈsɪstənt/ - English Meaning: A person who helps another person. - Vietnamese Meaning: Trợ lý. - Example: She works as a personal assistant. - Example Translation: Cô ấy làm trợ lý cá nhân. 180. associate - Type: Verb, Noun - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /əˈsoʊsieɪt/ - English Meaning: To connect one thing with another. - Vietnamese Meaning: Liên kết; cộng sự. - Example: Many people associate success with money. - Example Translation: Nhiều người liên hệ thành công với tiền bạc. 181. associated - Type: Adjective - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /əˈsoʊsieɪtɪd/ - English Meaning: Connected with something else. - Vietnamese Meaning: Liên quan. - Example: Stress is associated with poor sleep. - Example Translation: Căng thẳng có liên quan đến giấc ngủ kém. 182. association - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /əˌsoʊsiˈeɪʃən/ - English Meaning: A connection between things or people. - Vietnamese Meaning: Sự liên kết; hiệp hội. - Example: There is a strong association between exercise and health. - Example Translation: Có mối liên hệ chặt chẽ giữa tập thể dục và sức khỏe. 183. assume - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /əˈsuːm/ - English Meaning: To believe something without proof. - Vietnamese Meaning: Giả định. - Example: I assumed he knew the answer. - Example Translation: Tôi đã cho rằng anh ấy biết câu trả lời. 184. at - Type: Preposition - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /æt/, /ət/ - English Meaning: Used to show a place, time, or direction. - Vietnamese Meaning: Tại; ở. - Example: We met at the station. - Example Translation: Chúng tôi gặp nhau tại nhà ga. 185. athlete - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ˈæθliːt/ - English Meaning: A person who competes in sports. - Vietnamese Meaning: Vận động viên. - Example: The athlete trained every day. - Example Translation: Vận động viên tập luyện mỗi ngày. 186. atmosphere - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /ˈætməsfɪr/ - English Meaning: The feeling or mood of a place. - Vietnamese Meaning: Bầu không khí. - Example: The restaurant has a friendly atmosphere. - Example Translation: Nhà hàng có bầu không khí thân thiện. 187. attach - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /əˈtætʃ/ - English Meaning: To join one thing to another. - Vietnamese Meaning: Đính kèm; gắn vào. - Example: Please attach the file to your email. - Example Translation: Vui lòng đính kèm tệp vào email của bạn. 188. attack - Type: Noun, Verb - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /əˈtæk/ - English Meaning: To use force against someone or something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Tấn công. - Example: The army attacked at dawn. - Example Translation: Quân đội tấn công vào lúc bình minh. 189. attempt - Type: Noun, Verb - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /əˈtempt/ - English Meaning: An effort to do something difficult. - Vietnamese Meaning: Nỗ lực; cố gắng. - Example: He made an attempt to solve the problem. - Example Translation: Anh ấy đã cố gắng giải quyết vấn đề. 190. attend - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /əˈtend/ - English Meaning: To be present at an event. - Vietnamese Meaning: Tham dự. - Example: Many students attended the meeting. - Example Translation: Nhiều sinh viên đã tham dự cuộc họp. 191. attention - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /əˈtenʃən/ - English Meaning: Notice or focus given to something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Sự chú ý. - Example: Please pay attention to the instructions. - Example Translation: Vui lòng chú ý đến các hướng dẫn. 192. attitude - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /ˈætɪtuːd/ - English Meaning: A way of thinking or feeling about something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Thái độ. - Example: She has a positive attitude toward work. - Example Translation: Cô ấy có thái độ tích cực đối với công việc. 193. attorney - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: B2 - IPA (US): /əˈtɜːrni/ - English Meaning: A lawyer who represents clients in legal matters. - Vietnamese Meaning: Luật sư. - Example: The attorney prepared the legal documents. - Example Translation: Luật sư đã chuẩn bị các tài liệu pháp lý. 194. attract - Type: Verb - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /əˈtrækt/ - English Meaning: To make someone interested in something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Thu hút. - Example: The museum attracts many visitors. - Example Translation: Bảo tàng thu hút nhiều khách tham quan. 195. attraction - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: B1 - IPA (US): /əˈtrækʃən/ - English Meaning: Something that draws interest or attention. - Vietnamese Meaning: Điểm thu hút; sức hấp dẫn. - Example: This beach is a popular tourist attraction. - Example Translation: Bãi biển này là một điểm du lịch hấp dẫn. 196. attractive - Type: Adjective - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /əˈtræktɪv/ - English Meaning: Pleasant or appealing to look at. - Vietnamese Meaning: Hấp dẫn; thu hút. - Example: The city is attractive to tourists. - Example Translation: Thành phố rất hấp dẫn đối với khách du lịch. 197. audience - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ˈɔːdiəns/ - English Meaning: The people watching or listening to something. - Vietnamese Meaning: Khán giả. - Example: The audience enjoyed the performance. - Example Translation: Khán giả đã rất thích buổi biểu diễn. 198. audio - Type: Noun, Adjective - CEFR Level: A2 - IPA (US): /ˈɔːdioʊ/ - English Meaning: Related to sound or sound recording. - Vietnamese Meaning: Âm thanh. - Example: The audio quality is excellent. - Example Translation: Chất lượng âm thanh rất tuyệt vời. 199. August - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /ˈɔːɡəst/ - English Meaning: The eighth month of the year. - Vietnamese Meaning: Tháng Tám. - Example: We usually travel in August. - Example Translation: Chúng tôi thường đi du lịch vào tháng Tám. 200. aunt - Type: Noun - CEFR Level: A1 - IPA (US): /ænt/, /ɑːnt/ - English Meaning: The sister of a parent or the wife of an uncle. - Vietnamese Meaning: Cô; dì; thím; mợ. - Example: My aunt lives in Ho Chi Minh City. - Example Translation: Dì của tôi sống ở Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh.
questions.answerHtml:
Words 101 to 200 from the Oxford 3000 list - the 3000 most important words to learn in English from A1 to B2 level.

101. analysis

  • Type: Noun
  • CEFR Level: B1
  • IPA (US): /əˈnæləsɪs/
  • English Meaning: A detailed examination of something.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Sự phân tích.
  • Example: The analysis showed a rise in sales.
  • Example Translation: Bản phân tích cho thấy doanh số tăng lên.

102. analyze

  • Type: Verb
  • CEFR Level: A2
  • IPA (US): /ˈænəlaɪz/
  • English Meaning: To examine something carefully.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Phân tích.
  • Example: Scientists analyze the data.
  • Example Translation: Các nhà khoa học phân tích dữ liệu.

103. ancient

  • Type: Adjective
  • CEFR Level: A2
  • IPA (US): /ˈeɪnʃənt/
  • English Meaning: Very old and from a long time ago.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Cổ đại; cổ xưa.
  • Example: Egypt is famous for its ancient monuments.
  • Example Translation: Ai Cập nổi tiếng với các di tích cổ đại.

104. an

  • Type: Indefinite Article
  • CEFR Level: A1
  • IPA (US): /ən/, /æn/
  • English Meaning: Used before a singular noun beginning with a vowel sound.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Một.
  • Example: She is an engineer.
  • Example Translation: Cô ấy là một kỹ sư.

105. and

  • Type: Conjunction
  • CEFR Level: A1
  • IPA (US): /ənd/, /ænd/
  • English Meaning: Used to connect words or ideas.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Và.
  • Example: Tom and Mary are friends.
  • Example Translation: Tom và Mary là bạn bè.

106. anger

  • Type: Noun
  • CEFR Level: B2
  • IPA (US): /ˈæŋɡər/
  • English Meaning: A strong feeling of being upset.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Sự tức giận.
  • Example: His anger was easy to see.
  • Example Translation: Sự tức giận của anh ấy rất dễ nhận thấy.

107. angle

  • Type: Noun
  • CEFR Level: B2
  • IPA (US): /ˈæŋɡəl/
  • English Meaning: The space between two lines or surfaces.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Góc; khía cạnh.
  • Example: Look at the problem from a different angle.
  • Example Translation: Hãy nhìn vấn đề từ một góc độ khác.

108. angry

  • Type: Adjective
  • CEFR Level: A1
  • IPA (US): /ˈæŋɡri/
  • English Meaning: Feeling strong annoyance or displeasure.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Tức giận.
  • Example: She was angry about the mistake.
  • Example Translation: Cô ấy tức giận về sai lầm đó.

109. animal

  • Type: Noun
  • CEFR Level: A1
  • IPA (US): /ˈænɪməl/
  • English Meaning: A living creature that is not a human.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Động vật.
  • Example: The zoo has many animals.
  • Example Translation: Sở thú có nhiều loài động vật.

110. ankle

  • Type: Noun
  • CEFR Level: A2
  • IPA (US): /ˈæŋkəl/
  • English Meaning: The joint between the foot and the leg.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Mắt cá chân.
  • Example: He injured his ankle while running.
  • Example Translation: Anh ấy bị thương ở mắt cá chân khi chạy.

111. anniversary

  • Type: Noun
  • CEFR Level: B2
  • IPA (US): /ˌænɪˈvɜːrsəri/
  • English Meaning: The yearly celebration of an important event.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Ngày kỷ niệm.
  • Example: They celebrated their wedding anniversary.
  • Example Translation: Họ đã kỷ niệm ngày cưới.

112. announce

  • Type: Verb
  • CEFR Level: B1
  • IPA (US): /əˈnaʊns/
  • English Meaning: To make information public.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Thông báo; công bố.
  • Example: The company announced a new product.
  • Example Translation: Công ty đã công bố một sản phẩm mới.

113. announcement

  • Type: Noun
  • CEFR Level: B1
  • IPA (US): /əˈnaʊnsmənt/
  • English Meaning: A public statement containing information.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Thông báo.
  • Example: The announcement surprised everyone.
  • Example Translation: Thông báo đó khiến mọi người ngạc nhiên.

114. annoy

  • Type: Verb
  • CEFR Level: B1
  • IPA (US): /əˈnɔɪ/
  • English Meaning: To make someone slightly angry.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Làm khó chịu.
  • Example: Loud noises annoy me.
  • Example Translation: Tiếng ồn lớn làm tôi khó chịu.

115. annoyed

  • Type: Adjective
  • CEFR Level: B1
  • IPA (US): /əˈnɔɪd/
  • English Meaning: Feeling slightly angry.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Khó chịu; bực mình.
  • Example: She was annoyed with her brother.
  • Example Translation: Cô ấy bực mình với em trai mình.

116. annoying

  • Type: Adjective
  • CEFR Level: B1
  • IPA (US): /əˈnɔɪɪŋ/
  • English Meaning: Causing annoyance.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Gây khó chịu.
  • Example: It's annoying when people are late.
  • Example Translation: Thật khó chịu khi mọi người đến muộn.

117. annual

  • Type: Adjective
  • CEFR Level: B2
  • IPA (US): /ˈænjuəl/
  • English Meaning: Happening once every year.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Hàng năm.
  • Example: The company holds an annual meeting.
  • Example Translation: Công ty tổ chức cuộc họp thường niên.

118. another

  • Type: Determiner, Pronoun
  • CEFR Level: A1
  • IPA (US): /əˈnʌðər/
  • English Meaning: One more or a different one.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Một cái khác; thêm một.
  • Example: Could I have another cup of coffee?
  • Example Translation: Tôi có thể uống thêm một tách cà phê được không?

119. answer

  • Type: Noun, Verb
  • CEFR Level: A1
  • IPA (US): /ˈænsər/
  • English Meaning: A reply to a question.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Câu trả lời; trả lời.
  • Example: She answered all the questions correctly.
  • Example Translation: Cô ấy trả lời đúng tất cả các câu hỏi.

120. anxious

  • Type: Adjective
  • CEFR Level: B2
  • IPA (US): /ˈæŋkʃəs/
  • English Meaning: Worried or nervous about something.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Lo lắng.
  • Example: He felt anxious before the interview.
  • Example Translation: Anh ấy cảm thấy lo lắng trước buổi phỏng vấn.

121. any

  • Type: Determiner, Pronoun, Adverb
  • CEFR Level: A1
  • IPA (US): /ˈeni/
  • English Meaning: Used to refer to one or more things without being specific.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Bất kỳ; nào.
  • Example: Do you have any questions?
  • Example Translation: Bạn có câu hỏi nào không?

122. anybody

  • Type: Pronoun
  • CEFR Level: A2
  • IPA (US): /ˈenibɑːdi/
  • English Meaning: Any person.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Bất kỳ ai.
  • Example: Does anybody know the answer?
  • Example Translation: Có ai biết câu trả lời không?

123. anymore

  • Type: Adverb
  • CEFR Level: A2
  • IPA (US): /ˌeniˈmɔːr/
  • English Meaning: Any longer; now.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Nữa.
  • Example: I don't live there anymore.
  • Example Translation: Tôi không còn sống ở đó nữa.

124. anyone

  • Type: Pronoun
  • CEFR Level: A1
  • IPA (US): /ˈeniwʌn/
  • English Meaning: Any person.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Bất kỳ ai.

  • Type: Verb
  • CEFR Level: B1
  • IPA (US): /əˈtrækt/
  • English Meaning: To make someone interested in something.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Thu hút.

  • Example Translation: Bảo tàng thu hút nhiều khách tham quan.

195. attraction

  • Type: Noun
  • CEFR Level: B1
  • IPA (US): /əˈtrækʃən/

  • Vietnamese Meaning: Điểm thu hút; sức hấp dẫn.

  • Example Translation: Bãi biển này là một điểm du lịch hấp dẫn.

196. attractive

  • Type: Adjective
  • CEFR Level: A2
  • IPA (US): /əˈtræktɪv/
  • English Meaning: Pleasant or appealing to look at.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Hấp dẫn; thu hút.
  • Example: The city is attractive to tourists.
  • Example Translation: Thành phố rất hấp dẫn đối với khách du lịch.

197. audience

  • Type: Noun
  • CEFR Level: A2
  • IPA (US): /ˈɔːdiəns/
  • English Meaning: The people watching or listening to something.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Khán giả.
  • Example: The audience enjoyed the performance.
  • Example Translation: Khán giả đã rất thích buổi biểu diễn.

198. audio

  • Type: Noun, Adjective
  • CEFR Level: A2
  • IPA (US): /ˈɔːdioʊ/
  • English Meaning: Related to sound or sound recording.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Âm thanh.
  • Example: The audio quality is excellent.
  • Example Translation: Chất lượng âm thanh rất tuyệt vời.

199. August

  • Type: Noun
  • CEFR Level: A1
  • IPA (US): /ˈɔːɡəst/
  • English Meaning: The eighth month of the year.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Tháng Tám.
  • Example: We usually travel in August.
  • Example Translation: Chúng tôi thường đi du lịch vào tháng Tám.

200. aunt

  • Type: Noun
  • CEFR Level: A1
  • IPA (US): /ænt/, /ɑːnt/
  • English Meaning: The sister of a parent or the wife of an uncle.
  • Vietnamese Meaning: Cô; dì; thím; mợ.
  • Example: My aunt lives in Ho Chi Minh City.
